correctness.rationale: For the symmetric pair p_±=(1±x)/2, the two-copy input trace distance is exactly x while the normalized-square target distance is exactly 2x/(1+x^2). Triangle inequality plus CPTP contraction forces uniform error at least x(1-x^2)/(2(1+x^2)). Its unique interior maximum occurs at x^2=sqrt(5)-2. Discarding one copy has error |f(p)-p| equal to the same one-variable function, so the lower bound is attained. All quantifiers are analytic; computation is corroborative only.

value.rationale: The theorem turns a qualitative virtual-versus-physical distinction into a sharp operational boundary. Even an arbitrary deterministic CPTP process acting jointly on both copies cannot uniformly approximate the normalized square target below 15.014% trace distance, and the minimax-optimal strategy is simply to discard one copy. This is a natural benchmark for the source's one-round no-postselection setting rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
